Subject: Follow-up from today's call — dedicated pool & isolation initial asks

Thanks again for the time today. Quick notes from our side and what matters most for Glyph Health as we evaluate a reserved/dedicated offering: 

- Primary pain: production inference latency spikes during peak patient-matching windows (8–10am PT) and unpredictable tail latency when other teams run large batches. We need predictable p95/p99.
- Data isolation: patient PHI must remain logically isolated; we prefer either single-tenant pools or hardware-enforced isolation.
- Throughput target: sustained ~150 qps with brief peaks to 300 qps for short bursts.
- SLA ask: 99.9 availability, 200ms median latency for standard generation paths.
- Timeline: pilot in Q4 2026, production by end of Q1 2027.

Attaching a rough SOW and our standard security questionnaire (see attachments). Can you send a short options summary (reserved silo vs shared reserved with strong tenant isolation) and a ballpark cost / sizing estimate so procurement has something to review? Also open to a technical deep-dive with Ben and Priyom to validate KV cache approach and model constraints.

Thanks —
Alyssa Grant
Head of ML Ops, Glyph Health
alyssa@glyphhealth.com

Alyssa — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments. Short recap (so we're aligned) and proposed next steps: 

Recap of must-haves:
- Predictable p95/p99 during peak windows; avoid cross-tenant tail latency.
- Logical or hardware isolation for PHI workloads; SOC2 artifacts required for procurement.
- Baseline sustained throughput ~150 qps, peaks to 300 qps. SLA target ~99.9.

High-level options we'll propose:
1) Single-tenant dedicated pool (isolated nodes): strongest isolation, predictable latency, higher unit cost.
2) Reserved multi-tenant pool with strict QoS lanes and workload shaping: lower cost, still predictable with enforced isolation policies + prefix/KV cache partitioning.

Sizing & pilot suggestion:
- Pilot: 3-month reserved pool sized for sustained 150 qps — equivalent to 4 x A100-80GB-class instances (we'll provide model-specific vCPU/GPU baselines once Ben confirms models).
- Production ramp: scale to a 6–8 instance footprint with burst capacity for peak windows and autoscaling guardrails.

Next steps:
- Ben/Priyom: schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive (KV cache, model family, quantization, latency SLO testing).
- I'll send a short options deck + two cost scenarios (single-tenant vs multi-tenant reserved) and a pilot commercial term draft for procurement.
- Procurement: please share any PO timelines or required contract language.

Ben/Priyom — can you take a pass on sizing assumptions below and call out any red flags? I pasted the ask from Alyssa above.

Best,

Quick technical notes / questions from my side: 

- Model family & tokenization: Do you expect to run a single model (e.g., open-llama/13B) or multiple families? Multi-family increases memory footprint and reduces effective concurrency per GPU.
- KV cache retention: Are you using long-context KV caching across sessions (patient history) or short-term prefix caching? Long retention favors larger memory configs.
- Batch vs streaming mix: Is most traffic streaming (low-latency token streaming) or batched offline requests? Streaming needs smaller batch windows and affects throughput assumptions.
- Isolation: hardware-enforced single-tenant vs software QoS lanes? If we need hardware isolation we should plan for node-level allocation; that increases cost and reduces packing efficiency.

Sizing sketch (very preliminary):
- If single model, quantized, and mostly streaming: pilot = 4 x A100-80GB (sustained 150 qps). Production 6–8 nodes for headroom and burst.
- If multi-model family or long KV retention: pilot = 6 x A100-80GB equivalent.

I'll attach a quick CSV with assumptions and a runbook checklist for the deep-dive. Priyom — can you validate the SLO test harness items (p95 load profile, synthetic data, privacy-preserving traces)?

Attachment: inference-sizing-estimate.csv

Ben
